Quantify and report the uncertainty of isoform-level results

Source: R/uncertainty.R
uncertainty.Rd

An isoform-level result is only as good as the quantification behind it. Reads that map to several isoforms of a gene can be shared out between them in more than one way, so the estimate of each isoform carries an inferential uncertainty that is unrelated to biological variability. Salmon measures it by drawing replicates from the posterior (Gibbs sampling, --numGibbsSamples) and by writing the equivalence classes (--dumpEq). These functions turn that information into columns that describe each isoform and each call, to be reported next to the results.

Every isoform gets four kinds of evidence:

  • Quantification uncertainty: the inferential relative variance (mean_inf_rv, Zhu et al. 2019, as in fishpond), the variance of the replicates in excess of what counting noise alone would give, relative to the expression. Isoforms with a high value are not well determined by the reads. uncertain flags mean_inf_rv >= inf_rv_cutoff.

  • Ambiguity between isoforms: the correlation between the replicates of isoforms of the same gene. A strong negative correlation means the reads cannot tell the two isoforms apart and every read taken from one is given to the other. Pairs at or below cor_cutoff are ambiguous and are joined into ambiguity_groups that can be tested as one feature. This is the idea of mmcollapse (Turro et al. 2014), with a fixed cutoff.

  • Read support: the share of the fragments of an isoform that map to it alone (unique_fraction, from the equivalence classes).

  • Stability of the fold-change: the contrast between two groups is repeated on every replicate. lfc_lo/lfc_hi is the 95% interval of the log2 fold-change over replicates, sign_agreement the share of replicates that agree on its direction and frac_draws_sig the share in which the isoform is called differentially expressed.

de_confidence() repeats the contrast on every replicate. unstable flags a fold-change whose direction fewer than min_agreement (95%) of the replicates agree on, and unstable_de a call of the primary test with such a direction. The other columns describe the quantification of the isoform, and flags lists those that apply. None of them is a verdict on a call: report them next to it.

  • add_uncertainty(x, paths) reads the replicates, equivalence classes and run metadata from the Salmon output directories (or Oarfish output prefixes, see read_oarfish()) paths (named by sample ID, in any order), computes the tables below and stores them in the object, so that they are written by write_isoformic(). When group is given it also stores the fold-change stability of that contrast.

  • tx_uncertainty(x): per-transcript table, for the transcripts whose draws are in the object (the expressed ones).

  • isoform_ambiguity(x): per-pair table of replicate correlations.

  • de_confidence(x, group): per-feature table of fold-change stability, recomputed from the replicates; with collapse_groups = TRUE, ambiguous isoforms are summed into one feature before testing. Without group it returns the table that add_uncertainty(group = ) stored.

  • uncertainty_report(x): a list of summary tables for a methods or results section.

  • uncertainty_methods(x): a ready-to-edit paragraph that states the settings used.

The replicates themselves are kept in x@metadata$inf_reps, a list with one transcript x sample matrix per replicate. write_isoformic() writes them, one Parquet file per replicate, with the tables derived from them, and read_isoformic() restores them; with keep_draws = FALSE only the tables are kept and written. x[i, j] keeps the replicates of the kept transcripts and samples as a view: it shares the draws of x and records the selection, so the draws of x stay in memory while the subset exists (see the Subsetting section of IsoformicExperiment); to contrast two groups of a larger object, pass levels instead of subsetting. Draws are read only for the transcripts of x; with a counts assay, only for those with a mean count of at least min_count, and the others are treated as unexpressed.

Usage

add_uncertainty(
  self,
  paths = NULL,
  group = NULL,
  levels = NULL,
  n_draws = NULL,
  min_count = 1,
  inf_rv_cutoff = 0.5,
  cor_cutoff = -0.5,
  min_agreement = 0.95,
  equivalence = TRUE,
  identifiability = FALSE,
  run_qc = TRUE,
  keep_draws = TRUE,
  collapse_groups = FALSE,
  groups = NULL,
  ...
)

tx_uncertainty(self, gene_name = NULL, ...)

isoform_ambiguity(self, gene_name = NULL, ambiguous_only = FALSE, ...)

de_confidence(
  self,
  group = NULL,
  levels = NULL,
  collapse_groups = FALSE,
  gene_name = NULL,
  pseudocount = 5,
  inf_rv_cutoff = NULL,
  min_agreement = NULL,
  ...
)

uncertainty_report(self, ...)

uncertainty_methods(self, ...)

Arguments

self

An IsoformicExperiment.

paths

Salmon output directories or Oarfish output prefixes (see read_inferential_replicates()), named by sample ID. NULL uses the replicates already stored in the object.

group

Name of a col_data() column with the sample groups. In de_confidence(), NULL returns the stored table.

levels

The two group levels to contrast, reference first. Samples of other groups are left out of the contrast. NULL uses the levels of group, which must then be exactly two.

n_draws

Number of replicates to read; NULL reads all of them.

min_count

Minimum mean estimated count for a transcript to be assessed (and, with a counts assay, for its replicates to be read).

inf_rv_cutoff

Inferential relative variance from which an isoform is called uncertain. In de_confidence(), NULL uses the value the tables were computed with; without group, a value recomputes the "uncertain quantification" flag of the stored table. It describes the isoform and is not used to judge calls.

cor_cutoff

Mean replicate correlation at or below which two isoforms of a gene are called ambiguous: a number, or "adaptive" to derive it from the data as mmcollapse does (minus the 97.5th percentile of the largest mean correlation of each isoform, which treats the positive correlations as noise). The value used is stored and stated by uncertainty_methods().

min_agreement

Share of replicates that must agree on the direction of a fold-change; below it the fold-change is flagged unstable. In de_confidence(), NULL uses the stored value; without group, a value recomputes unstable, flags and unstable_de of the stored table from its sign_agreement, without the replicates.

equivalence

Logical, read the equivalence classes when present, or the table returned by equivalence_support(), to attach read support when the draws are supplied without paths.

identifiability

Logical, also compute which transcripts the equivalence classes can tell apart (equivalence_identifiability(); minutes per sample, needs paths and, for human samples, the Matrix package), or the table that function returned. de_confidence() then reports identifiable.

run_qc

Logical, add the run metadata of Salmon or Oarfish (see salmon_run_qc()) to col_data(), with the column names prefixed by salmon_ or oarfish_.

keep_draws

Logical, keep the replicates in the object (needed to recompute the tables, for de_confidence(group = ), inferential_overdispersion() and the uncertainty of productive_fraction()). Kept replicates are also written by write_isoformic().

collapse_groups

Logical, sum ambiguous isoforms into one feature before testing the contrast.

groups

External groups of transcripts that the reads cannot tell apart, replacing the groups built from the correlation of the replicates: a table with transcript_id and group_id, or the path to Terminus output (see read_terminus_groups()), or the cut of TreeTerminus trees (see cut_transcript_trees()). ambiguous and collapse_groups then follow these groups; the pairs of isoform_ambiguity() keep describing the correlation.

...

Not used; reserved for methods.

gene_name

Optional gene names or IDs to keep.

ambiguous_only

Logical, isoform_ambiguity() returns only the ambiguous pairs.

pseudocount

Pseudocount of the log2 fold-change (5, as in swish).

Value

  • add_uncertainty(): the object with dea$uncertainty, dea$ambiguity and, when group is given, dea$confidence filled in.

  • tx_uncertainty(): a tibble with transcript_id, gene_id, gene_name, transcript_name, transcript_type, mean_count, assessed (mean_count >= min_count; the statistics are NA for the others), mean_inf_rv, max_inf_rv, mean_inf_cv, uncertain, min_sibling_cor, n_ambiguous_partners, ambiguity_group and, when equivalence classes were read, n_classes, n_fragments, n_unique_fragments, unique_fraction and low_information (TRUE for an uncertain isoform without a single fragment of its own, the isoforms mmcollapse selects for collapsing). With identifiability, also identifiable_fraction and identifiable.

  • isoform_ambiguity(): a tibble of isoform pairs of the same gene, sorted by mean_cor, with gene_id, gene_name, transcript_id_1, transcript_id_2, mean_cor, min_cor, n_samples, collapse_gain, ambiguous, transcript_name_1 and transcript_name_2. collapse_gain is the score Terminus groups on (Sarkar et al. 2020): the inferential relative variance of the sum of the two isoforms minus the mean of their own, averaged over samples. The more negative, the more is gained by testing the pair as one feature.

  • de_confidence(): a tibble with one row per feature, sorted by the absolute median fold-change: feature_id, feature_type ("transcript" or "group"), gene_id, gene_name, transcript_ids (the members, separated by ;), transcript_name, transcript_type, mean_count, the fold-change over the replicates (lfc_median, lfc_lo, lfc_hi, lfc_sd), sign_agreement, frac_draws_effect (share of replicates that agree on the direction with an absolute fold-change of at least the cutoff of de_cutoffs()), frac_draws_sig, mean_inf_rv (NA for a feature that is not assessed, which is then never flagged as uncertain), ambiguous, identifiable (only when the identifiability was computed; NA for groups), flags (the descriptive flags that apply, separated by "; ": "unstable direction", "uncertain quantification", "ambiguous with a sibling isoform", "not identifiable from the equivalence classes"; NA when none applies), the current differential expression result (det_log2FC, det_qvalue, n_det_sig, the number of significant members; read from de_tx() each time, so they follow de_tx<- and de_cutoffs()) and unstable_de, TRUE for a feature with a significant member and an unstable direction (NA without stored results). unstable (after sign_agreement) is sign_agreement < min_agreement, NA for a feature that is not assessed. The sign agreement is measured against the median sign over the replicates, not against det_log2FC.

  • uncertainty_report(): a list with settings (a list of the cutoffs), and the tibbles replicates (replicate_type, n_draws, resampling_df, the degrees of freedom over the study, and median_overdispersion, NA unless the draws are in the object and close to 1 for long reads), run (the run metadata in col_data()), transcripts (by transcript type, with median_inf_rv, q25_inf_rv and q75_inf_rv), genes, de (significant features per flag; the flags describe the calls and are not a verdict: one row per flag, unstable first, with flag, rule, n_significant, n_assessed, n_flagged and pct_flagged; a collapsed group with a significant member counts once, and is never ambiguous, since its members were summed) and switches (genes with isoform switches, all and without unstable directions: n_genes, n_opposite_direction and n_det_not_deg). run and de are NULL when their input is missing; switches needs only the transcript-level table (de_tx()) and is NULL without it, its "without unstable directions" row is NA without the fold-change stability of add_uncertainty(group = ), and its n_det_not_deg is NA without a gene-level table (de_gene()).

  • uncertainty_methods(): a character string.

Details

What the evidence supports. In a genome-wide evaluation on a placenta cohort (GENCODE 50, 30 Gibbs draws; see the article "Is quantification uncertainty worth checking?"), calls with an unstable direction replicated less often in held-out halves of the cohort than the other calls (35% against 64% pooled; odds ratio 0.36, 95% interval 0.31 to 0.41 with genes resampled as clusters, adjusted for count, test statistic, number of isoforms of the gene and transcript type; the interval is for that cohort and does not include the choice of samples). Their raw replication rate was lower in all 60 directed comparisons (30 half-splits of the same samples, each used in both directions); against flags of the same size made of the lowest-count or lowest-|z| calls, the gap was larger in all 60. The flag marked 6% of the calls and only about 10% of the calls that failed to replicate, so a stable direction is not evidence that a call is right: in comparisons of control samples, 93% of the false calls had a stable direction. The flag was a secondary measure of that evaluation, chosen as the headline after the results; its threshold of 0.95 was fixed in advance and no other was tried, and other primary tests (DESeq2, swish) and long-read bootstraps were not evaluated. Ambiguity predicted replication little (odds ratio 0.87); isoforms not identifiable from the equivalence classes, or in the top third of InfRV, replicated somewhat less (0.56 and 0.63). An InfRV of at least 0.5 marked 87% of the expressed isoforms.

The thresholds are heuristics, not universal constants. min_agreement = 0.95 is the threshold of that evaluation. It is a share of the replicates: with fewer than 20 replicates no replicate may disagree, with 30 one may, and with 100 five may. inf_rv_cutoff = 0.5 marks inferential relative variance above the sampling noise of about 30 draws: with 30 draws, sampling noise alone puts the value of a well-determined, highly expressed transcript near 0.1, while poorly determined isoforms typically reach several units. It describes the isoform and is not used to judge calls. cor_cutoff (-0.5) defines the ambiguity groups and the features of collapse_groups. Rerun with other cutoffs if the data call for it. The replicates measure the uncertainty of the quantification only; they do not replace biological replicates and cannot make a noisy contrast significant.

lfc_lo-lfc_hi is the spread of the screening statistic over the replicates, not a confidence interval for the point estimate of the primary test; for low counts that estimate can lie outside it. The sign agreement is measured against the sign of the median fold-change over the replicates (lfc_median), not against det_log2FC.

What is not measured. The replicates describe how much an estimate moves under the quantification model. They do not find the transcripts whose abundance is not identifiable, that is, where several abundance vectors explain the reads equally well (Zheng et al. 2022 report that only about half of the transcripts flagged by replicate variance are also non-identifiable in that sense), and they do not find an estimate that is wrong because the annotation lacks the transcript the reads came from (Ma and Kingsford 2019). An ambiguous pair is a statement about the replicates, not a proof of non-identifiability.

How many replicates. The inferential relative variance and the correlations are computed per sample, from the replicates of that sample. The overdispersion used to scale counts (see inferential_overdispersion()) pools all samples, and its precision depends on the total n_samples * (n_replicates - 1): Baldoni, Chen and Smyth (2024) recommend at least 60 and prefer 200 to 300, and find that Gibbs samples resolve low counts better than bootstrap replicates. add_uncertainty() says so when the total is below 60.

Fold-changes are computed on counts scaled to a common library size, as the difference between the groups of the mean of log2(scaled count + pseudocount), with a pseudocount of 5 (the swish convention): a log ratio of geometric means, on the scale of the per-replicate test, a Welch t-test on that log scale with Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment across features. It is not the log ratio of the arithmetic group means, and the two can differ in sign when one sample dominates a group. This is a screening statistic for stability, not a replacement for the primary test (swish, DESeq2, ...), whose results are shown next to it. When the sample table (col_data) has a library_size column, with the total estimated count of the full quantification, it is used for the scaling. Set it when the object holds only a subset of the transcripts, so that the subset does not change the scaling.

References

Zhu, A., Srivastava, A., Ibrahim, J.G., Patro, R., Love, M.I. (2019). Nonparametric expression analysis using inferential replicate counts. Nucleic Acids Research 47(18), e105.

Sarkar, H., Srivastava, A., Bravo, H.C., Love, M.I., Patro, R. (2020). Terminus enables the discovery of data-driven, robust transcript groups from RNA-seq data. Bioinformatics 36(Suppl 1), i102-i110.

Turro, E., Astle, W.J., Tavare, S. (2014). Flexible analysis of RNA-seq data using mixed effects models. Bioinformatics 30(2), 180-188.

Zheng, H., Ma, C., Kingsford, C. (2022). Deriving ranges of optimal estimated transcript expression due to nonidentifiability. Journal of Computational Biology 29(2), 121-139.

Ma, C., Kingsford, C. (2019). Detecting, categorizing, and correcting coverage anomalies of RNA-seq quantification. Cell Systems 9(6), 589-599.

Baldoni, P.L., Chen, L., Smyth, G.K. (2024). Faster and more accurate assessment of differential transcript expression with Gibbs sampling and edgeR v4. NAR Genomics and Bioinformatics 6(4), lqae151.

Examples

quant_dirs <- list.files(
  system.file("extdata", "mini_quants", package = "isoformic"),
  full.names = TRUE
)
names(quant_dirs) <- sub("_quant$", "", basename(quant_dirs))
annot <- system.file("extdata", "mini_annotation", package = "isoformic")
col_data <- data.frame(
  sample_id = names(quant_dirs),
  condition = rep(c("preeclampsia", "control"), each = 3)
)
iso <- read_salmon(quant_dirs, annot_path = annot, col_data = col_data)

# With your own data, `read_salmon(dirs, annot, inferential = TRUE)` or
# `add_uncertainty(iso, paths = dirs)` read the replicates that
# `salmon quant --numGibbsSamples 30` wrote; here bundled draws are used
draws <- as_inferential_replicates(read_parquet(
  system.file("extdata", "mini_draws.parquet", package = "isoformic")
))
iso@metadata$inf_reps <- draws
iso <- add_uncertainty(iso, group = "condition")
head(tx_uncertainty(iso))
#> # A tibble: 6 × 14
#>   transcript_id     gene_id gene_name transcript_name transcript_type mean_count

#> 4 ENST00000490885.6 ENSG00… PTGS2     PTGS2-203       retained_intron       8.98

isoform_ambiguity(iso, ambiguous_only = TRUE)
